summary: The article presents Fortran-90 as a base for parallel programming and describes the High Performance Fortran extensions, including data mapping directives, parallel statements and the extrinsic procedure interface. It also describes the HPF subset and lists capabilities left for later work, and it reports no experiments.
why_read: It explains the HPF data mapping model and its design trade-offs in plain terms, for a reader new to data-parallel Fortran.
main_contribution: A description of the HPF extensions to Fortran-90, with the rationale for its two-level alignment and distribution model.
main_limitation: The article describes a language design without an implementation or measurements, and it lists irregular and user-defined distributions among the missing capabilities.
